newsitem.title: SPAIN: Iberia warns unions at Venezuelan unit.
newsitem.headline: Iberia warns unions at Venezuelan unit.

text.p: Spanish airline Iberia refuses to invest another peseta in its loss-making Venezuelan subsidiary Viasa unless unions agree to a restructuring plan, and is prepared to see the carrier close down if there is no agreement, the chairman of the Spanish state holding company SEPI said.
"Viasa workers systematically reject any plan for the company," Pedro Ferreras told journalists at a reception at SEPI headquarters on Monday.
"We are not going to put in another peseta...Either we negotiate a serious restructuring plan or the company closes down. It couldn't be clearer," he added.

Iberia, which has invested nearly $120 million in Viasa since buying a 45 percent stake in 1991, agreed a plan with Viasa's other main shareholders in November under which the subsidiary would cut jobs, freeze pay and discard unprofitable routes.
The deal involved Iberia writing off some of Viasa's debt and the Venezuelan state holding company FIV, which owns 40 percent of the shares, funding the job cuts.
This, Iberia said, would return Viasa to profit in 1997.
